newsitem.title: USA: Omni says auditor issues qualified opinion.
newsitem.headline: Omni says auditor issues qualified opinion.

text.p: Omni Multimedia Group Inc said on Tuesday that it received a qualified going concern opinion for fiscal 1997 from its auditor, Price Waterhouse.
In addition, the company said it was late on about $1.5 million of its payments to a number of secured lenders and is working out extended terms with those institutions.
Omni also said it had been informed by the American Stock Exchange that it no longer meets the exchange's continual listing guidelines and that there was no assurance the listing can be continued.

Projecting into the second quarter of fiscal 1998, the turnkey software manufacturing company said it expected its operating results to be at or close to break-even. And for the last half of fiscal 1998, Omni said it expected operating results to be profitable.
"Sales are continuing to increase at Omni East and its 4CDs subsidiary is experiencing escalating sales from its encrypted Try-Before-You-Buy program," the company said in justifying its projections.
To further improve cash flow and operating results, the company said it was negotiating with several lending institutions to refinance its term loans, capital lease obligations and line of credit.
"The company has reduced its work force and has implemented pay cuts for all executives," Omni said in statement.
"This, combined with the reduction of other operating expenses and the elimination of the West Coast and Mid-West facilities has cut operating costs by over $4 million on an annualized basis."
